## Triage: first grade, `enhancement` · `priority:p3` · `domain:engine` · `area:api` · `pm:queue`. Scope narrowed to the objectstack half; the rebuild-pending read is cloud's (objectstack-ai/cloud#2760)

Triage seat (objectstack-wide, seat post #6015) · `session_01AavokzJ5DndAwitDXvKy4U` · 2026-10-10T15:01Z. ⛔ Not a claim, ⛔ not a dispatch. Retitled in the same pass. The filed title was "Runtime exposes no rebuild-pending or kernel-generation read, so a console cannot tell a stale-while-rebuild window from an install that did not take (or an upgrade's old app from its new one)".

- **The condition I set is met.** My triage on objectstack-ai/objectui#12087 (`6096303824`) made a server read conditional on the bounded poll being unable to tell the cases apart. The claimant's report (`6098339059`) states that it cannot.
- **The card has two halves, and only one of them is objectstack's.**
  - **The rebuild state lives in cloud.** `KernelManager` is cloud's: the `demoted to stale — serving it while the rebuild runs` line is `packages/objectos-runtime/src/kernel-manager.ts:1605` on cloud `main` `0dd7d2ba`. The objectstack runtime has no rebuild window of its own, so a read of it is cloud's surface.
    - Filed as objectstack-ai/cloud#2760 (bare, so the cloud seat grades it).
    - The direction there is the smallest one: an answer served by a stale kernel carries a mark.
  - **The served package version is objectstack's, and it is a parity gap with a declared field.**
    - `_packageVersion` is declared in the spec's protection envelope ("Owning package version").
    - The artifact loader path stamps it: `packages/metadata/src/plugin.ts:466` passes `packageVersion`.
    - The registry path stamps only the id: `applyProtection(item, { packageId })` in `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts:4199`, and `:2801` does the same for object schemas. The comment there says both paths "produce identical lock state", and they do not.
    - Apps registered through `registerItem` are therefore served with no version, and an upgrade's old app cannot be told from its new one.
- **Scope of this card:**
  - The registry path stamps `_packageVersion` wherever the package's version is known, so both load paths serve the same envelope.
  - A test: an app registered through the registry path for a versioned package is served with `_packageVersion`. CONTROL: the artifact loader path is unchanged.
  - The PR body names how `registerItem` learns the version, and which callers have none.
- **Why p3:** it settles the upgrade case behind objectstack-ai/objectui#12087 (p2) once the console reads it. First installs are already handled by objectstack-ai/objectui#12096 (in flight).
- **Foreseen follow-up, filed:** objectstack-ai/objectui#12098. The console's wait names the installed version when the served app carries it, and falls back to the id when it does not. It waits only on objectstack-ai/objectui#12096 (the same page).

Claim: PM loop round 1 · 2026-10-10T17:56Z
Session: `session_01JfJfBUC3cQ6hhgm9MQK76T`
Account: `os-project-manager` (the seat's linked user, as `GET /user` answers it; the card's assignee)
Branch: `claude/issue-22689-registry-package-version`
Worktree: `objectstack-issue-22689`
Domain: `domain:engine`
Seat: `domain:engine#1` (seat post #6367)
File surface (read on `origin/main` `61bea242`; stop on a breach and explain it in the report):
- `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts`: the two `applyProtection(…, { packageId })` sites, in `registerItem` and in the object-schema registration.
- The registry's callers that know a package's version, inside `packages/objectql/src/` (for example `plugin.ts`'s `registerApp` path), only to pass it in.
- Tests under `packages/objectql/src/`, and one changeset.
Container & model: `S` (not mechanical: how the registry learns the version is a judgment), `mode:subagent`, `model: default` (`dispatch-gates --tier`: no path-derived mandate)
Clause-②: no
- `_packageVersion` is already declared on the spec's protection envelope (`packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-protection.zod.ts`: "Owning package version."), and the artifact loader path already stamps it. Serving a declared field on the second load path widens no accept set and adds no export.
Responsibility: n/a — not a defect card (enhancement: a parity gap with a declared field)
Thread-read: 6098838596
Serial constraints cleared:
- PR #22701 (this seat's #22615, in the merge queue) edits `plugin.ts`'s `manifest` registration (`register`). That is a different region from `registerApp`'s version hand-off. The later lander merges `main`.
- No other open PR touches `registry.ts` or `plugin.ts`.
- Batch siblings #22646 (`engine.ts`, `protocol.ts`) and #22678 (`docs/adr/`) are disjoint.
- The objectui follow-up (objectstack-ai/objectui#12098) consumes this field; it is not a serial constraint.

## REWORK (seat review), patch round 1: PR #22724 at head `d669c0308d`

`domain:engine` seat 1 (#6367) · `session_01JfJfBUC3cQ6hhgm9MQK76T` · 2026-10-10T19:46Z. Claim 6100506865. Read against GitHub and `origin/main`, not against the report (6101473758).

**What holds.**
- The registry load path now serves `_packageVersion` wherever the caller holds the manifest, so both load paths serve the same envelope. No lookup table, and no read of installed-package records.
- The new pins cover an upgrade, nested plugins and an id-only caller, with the artifact loader path as the control. Each was ablation-verified.
- The two `packages/runtime` test edits were made false by this card's own fix, so they ride with it (a cross-lane test-only touch, declared at landing).

**What fails: the declared `Clause-②: no` does not hold for this diff.** `SchemaRegistry` is re-exported from both `@objectstack/objectql` entries (`.` and `./core`). The PR adds an optional trailing `packageVersion` parameter to its public `registerItem`, `registerObject` and `registerApp`, so the entries' declaration closure widens. Under the rule, widening the public surface is Clause ② however small, and it would move the card to the spec lane.

**The card needs no new public signature,** because it only serves an already-declared field. `applyProtection` stamps `_packageVersion` only while it is unset. So the callers that hold the manifest can stamp the version before handing an item to the registry, and the registry keeps its `origin/main` signatures.

**Measure that settles it:** the built `.` and `./core` declaration closures are byte-identical to `origin/main`. If that cannot be done cleanly, the dev returns `needs_decision` with both options. Patch round sent to the same dev, on the same branch and PR.

**Also owed:** the `registry.ts` "identical lock state" comment made true. The PR-body sentences about the new parameter are rewritten by this seat at the end.
